'''Lee M. Spetner''' ({{Langx|he|לי ספטנר}}; January 17, 1927 – August 9, 2024) was an American and Israeli [[creationist]] author, [[mechanical engineer]], applied [[biophysicist]], and [[physicist]], known best for his disagreements with the [[modern synthesis (20th century)|modern synthesis]]. In spite of his opposition to [[neo-Darwinism]], Spetner accepted a form of [[Orthogenesis|non-random evolution]] outlined in his 1996 book "Not By Chance! Shattering the Modern Theory of Evolution".<ref>"Not by Chance: Shattering the Modern Theory of Evolution". 1997 Lee Spetner. {{ISBN|978-1-880582-24-4}}</ref>

==Biography==
===Education===
Spetner received his BS degree in mechanical engineering from the [[McKelvey School of Engineering]] at [[Washington University in St. Louis]] in 1945<ref name="worldscientific">[https://web.archive.org/web/20101225020649/http://www.worldscibooks.com/etextbook/6998/6998_biograhies.pdf Worldscientific Biographies] Retrieved December 2010</ref> and his Ph.D. in physics from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]] in 1950, where his Ph.D. thesis advisors were Robert Williams and [[Bruno Rossi]].<ref name="alumni2008">[http://web.mit.edu/physics/news/physicsatmit/physicsatmit_08_alumninotes.pdf MIT Alumni report 2008] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100215170558/http://web.mit.edu/physics/news/physicsatmit/physicsatmit_08_alumninotes.pdf |date=2010-02-15 }} Retrieved December 2010</ref>

===Career===
Spetner continued to study at the [[Applied Physics Laboratory]] at [[Johns Hopkins University]] from 1951 to 1970, working on guided-missile systems. In 1970, he became technical director of Eljim, Ltd., later a subsidiary of [[Elbit Systems|Elbit, Ltd.]] in [[Ness Ziona|Nes Tsiona]], Israel, where he was a manager, a period that lasted a further 20 years.<ref name="worldscientific" /><ref name="borhatorah">[http://www.borhatorah.org/editions/14/bio-spetner.htm Biography of Lee M. Spetner at B'Or Ha'Torah] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110725094302/http://www.borhatorah.org/editions/14/bio-spetner.htm |date=2011-07-25 }} Retrieved December 2010</ref> His work here was on military electronic systems, including electronic countermeasures, and a military electronic navigation system.<ref name="worldscientific" />

He taught courses at Johns Hopkins University, [[Howard University]] and the [[Weizmann Institute]], including classical mechanics, electromagnetic theory, real-variable theory, probability theory, and statistical communication theory.<ref name="worldscientific" />

Spetner first became interested in [[evolution]] in the 1960s during a fellowship in the Department of Biophysics at Johns Hopkins University.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Not by Chance: Shattering the Modern Theory of Evolution|last=Spetner|first=Lee M.|publisher=Judaica Press|year=1997|isbn=1-880582-24-4|pages=ix}}</ref>  He wrote that he was skeptical of evolutionary theory because of his religious views and because of his intuition about how information in living organisms could have developed. Spetner published several papers on the subject of evolution between 1964 and 1970.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=1964|title=Natural selection: an information-transmission mechanism for evolution|journal=Journal of Theoretical Biology|volume=7|issue=3|pages=412–429|doi=10.1016/0022-5193(64)90014-1|pmid=5875346|last1=Spetner|first1=L.M.|bibcode=1964JThBi...7..412S }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=1966|title=Mutation -- a pacemaker for evolution|journal=Proceedings 2nd International Congress on Biophysics, Vienna}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=1968|title=Information transmission in evolution|journal=IEEE Transactions on Information Theory|volume=IT-14: 3|pages=3–6|doi=10.1109/tit.1968.1054070|last1=Spetner|first1=L.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=1970|title=Natural selection versus gene uniqueness|journal=Nature|volume=226|issue=5249|pages=948–949|doi=10.1038/226948a0|pmid=5445877|last1=Spetner|first1=L. M.|bibcode=1970Natur.226..948S|s2cid=4201339}}</ref> In Israel, he continued searching for evidence that contradicted the modern evolutionary synthesis. Spetner was inspired by Rabbi [[David Luria]] (1798–1855), who calculated that, according to [[Talmudic]] sources, there were 365 originally created species of [[Animal|beasts]] and 365 of [[birds]]. Spetner developed what he called his "nonrandom evolutionary hypothesis," which proposed rapid [[microevolution]] (which he attributed to a "built-in ability" in animals and plants to "respond adaptively to environmental stimuli"), and suggested that even some cases of [[macroevolution]] could be explained by his hypothesis.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite book|title=The Evolution Revolution|last=Spetner|first=Lee M.|publisher=Judaica Press|year=2014|isbn=978-1-60763-155-2|pages=102–105}}</ref> Spetner's critical stance on the plausibility of the evolutionary theory of the appearance of beneficial mutations was supported by the Australian statistician Professor [[Michael Hasofer]].<ref>Hasofer, A.M. [https://borhatorah.files.wordpress.com/2013/11/a-statistician-looks-at-neo-darwinism.pdf "A Statistician Looks at Neo-Darwinism."] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190111121658/https://borhatorah.files.wordpress.com/2013/11/a-statistician-looks-at-neo-darwinism.pdf |date=2019-01-11 }} ''B'Or Ha'Torah'' Vol. 3. (1983): 13-21.</ref><ref>Hasofer, A. M. "A simplified treatment of Spetner's natural selection model." ''Journal of Theoretical Biology'' 11, no. 2 (1966): 338-342.</ref>

Spetner, an avowed theist, has been described as a [[Jewish]] [[Creationist]].<ref>Tom McIver, Anti-evolution: an annotated bibliography, 2008 p. 277</ref> However, his Non Random Evolutionary Hypothesis is, in fact, agnostic. It makes no claim that scientific evidence proves a supernatural creator.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Not by Chance: Shattering the Modern Theory of Evolution|last=Spetner|first=Lee M.|publisher=Judaica Press|year=1997|isbn=1-880582-24-4|pages=212}}</ref> Additionally, Spetner vehemently rejected the teaching of Creation in public schools, asserting that "the subject is best handled in the home or within a religious environment."<ref>{{Cite book|title=The Evolution Revolution |last=Spetner |first=Lee M.|publisher=Judaica Press|year=2014 |isbn=978-1-60763-155-2|pages=138}}</ref> In 1980, at a conference for [[Jewish]] [[scientists]], Spetner claimed that [[Archaeopteryx]] was a fraud. Spetner continued his attack on the [[modern synthesis (20th century)|modern synthesis]] in his book ''Not by chance! Shattering the Modern Theory of Evolution''.<ref>Randy Moore, Mark Decker, Sehoya Cotner, Chronology of the evolution-creationism controversy, 2010, pp. 286 - 287.</ref>

Spetner was a critic of the role of [[mutations]] in the modern synthesis. Spetner claimed that random mutations lead to a loss of [[genetic information]] and that there is no scientific evidence to support common descent:

{{quote|We see then that the mutation reduces the specificity of the ribosome protein and that means a loss of genetic information. ... Rather than saying the bacterium gained resistance to the antibiotic, it is more correct to say that is lost sensitivity to it. ... All point mutations that have been studied on the molecular level turn out to reduce the genetic information and not increase it.|Lee Spetner|Not by Chance, Shattering the Modern Theory of Evolution<ref>Lee Spetner, Not by Chance, Shattering the Modern Theory of Evolution, 1996, pp 131 - 138</ref>}}

Spetner continued to study after retirement, pursuing interests in evolution<ref name="borhatorah" /> and cancer cures.<ref name="alumni2008" />

Spetner's last book "The Evolution Revolution: Why Thinking People are Rethinking Evolution" develops his nonrandom hypothesis (NREH) and was published in 2014 by Judaica Press.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=The Evolution Revolution|website=Judaica Press}}</ref>

===Death===
Spetner died in Jerusalem on August 9, 2024, at the age of 97.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://baltimorejewishlife.com/news/news-detail.php?SECTION_ID=1&ARTICLE_ID=174020 |title=BDE: Dr. Lee Spetner, Z'L |date=August 11, 2024 |website=BaltimoreJewishLife.com |access-date=August 12, 2024}}</ref>
